 Dreo Electric Heater Recall — 340,000 Units Recalled Due to Fire Risk
 Nov 15, 2026 7:16 PM PST 
 [Photo] Dreo electric heater model DR-HSH015 
 Recently, according to the Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC), Dreo announced a recall of approximately 338,800 units of its Dreo electric heater model ‘DR-HSH015’ due to the risk of catching fire from overheating.
 To date, a total of 17 reports have been received of the products catching fire. Among these, 3 cases led to property damage, and 1 case was confirmed as a burn injury to the hand.
 The recall targets products manufactured between April 2025 and January 2026. It is a black ceramic electric heater measuring approximately 11.5 inches wide and 13 inches high, and includes a remote control.
 The affected products were sold from September 2025 to October 2026 at Costco stores nationwide and online shopping malls such as Dreo, Best Buy, Kohl’s, Lowe’s, and The Home Depot for $70 to $110. The CPSC recommended that consumers immediately stop using the product and contact the manufacturer for a free replacement.
 Consumers must unplug the power plug, cut the cord following the instructions to dispose of the product, and submit a photograph of the discarded unit.
 Inquiries regarding the recall can be made by phone at 833-820-0887 or via the website at recallrtr.com/spaceheater.
